knowledge_point.title: Finding the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface

question.:question/problem:
Find the surface area of the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle u,v - 2,- u + 2 v + 1\rangle.
$$

For $1\le u\le 2$ and $1\le v\le 4$.

The tangent vectors are $\mathbf r_u=\langle 1,0,-1\rangle$ and $\mathbf r_v=\langle 0,1,2\rangle$. Use

$$
A(S)=\iint_D\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm dA.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a parametrization over $D$, use $$
A(S)=\iint_D\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm dA
$$

Differentiate and form the fundamental vector product:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf r_u&=\langle 1,0,-1\rangle,\\\mathbf r_v&=\langle 0,1,2\rangle,\\\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\1&0&-1\\0&1&2\end{vmatrix}\\&=\langle 1,-2,1\rangle.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|=\sqrt{(1)^2+(-2)^2+(1)^2}=\sqrt{6}.
$$

The parameter rectangle has side lengths $2-(1)=1$ and $4-(1)=3$, so its area is $3$.

The area scale factor is constant, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(S)&=\iint_D \sqrt{6}\,\mathrm dA\\&=\sqrt{6}\cdot\operatorname{Area}(D)\\&=\sqrt{6}\cdot(3)=3 \sqrt{6}.
\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface

question.:question/problem:
Find the surface area of the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle u - 1,v - 1,u + 2 v + 1\rangle.
$$

For $-1\le u\le 0$ and $-2\le v\le 0$.

The tangent vectors are $\mathbf r_u=\langle 1,0,1\rangle$ and $\mathbf r_v=\langle 0,1,2\rangle$. Use

$$
A(S)=\iint_D\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm dA.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a parametrization over $D$, use $$
A(S)=\iint_D\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm dA
$$

Differentiate and form the fundamental vector product:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf r_u&=\langle 1,0,1\rangle,\\\mathbf r_v&=\langle 0,1,2\rangle,\\\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\1&0&1\\0&1&2\end{vmatrix}\\&=\langle -1,-2,1\rangle.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|=\sqrt{(-1)^2+(-2)^2+(1)^2}=\sqrt{6}.
$$

The parameter rectangle has side lengths $0-(-1)=1$ and $0-(-2)=2$, so its area is $2$.

The area scale factor is constant, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(S)&=\iint_D \sqrt{6}\,\mathrm dA\\&=\sqrt{6}\cdot\operatorname{Area}(D)\\&=\sqrt{6}\cdot(2)=2 \sqrt{6}.
\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface

question.:question/problem:
Find the surface area of the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle u + 2,v,- 2 u - 2 v + 1\rangle.
$$

For $1\le u\le 3$ and $-1\le v\le 1$.

The tangent vectors are $\mathbf r_u=\langle 1,0,-2\rangle$ and $\mathbf r_v=\langle 0,1,-2\rangle$. Use

$$
A(S)=\iint_D\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm dA.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a parametrization over $D$, use $$
A(S)=\iint_D\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm dA
$$

Differentiate and form the fundamental vector product:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf r_u&=\langle 1,0,-2\rangle,\\\mathbf r_v&=\langle 0,1,-2\rangle,\\\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\1&0&-2\\0&1&-2\end{vmatrix}\\&=\langle 2,2,1\rangle.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|=\sqrt{(2)^2+(2)^2+(1)^2}=3.
$$

The parameter rectangle has side lengths $3-(1)=2$ and $1-(-1)=2$, so its area is $4$.

The area scale factor is constant, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(S)&=\iint_D 3\,\mathrm dA\\&=3\cdot\operatorname{Area}(D)\\&=3\cdot(4)=12.
\end{aligned}
$$
